chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamza who said:

Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) was asked — and I was present — about the woman who sees the yellowness (sufra). So he said: 'Whatever occurred before the menstruation (haydh) is part of the menstruation, and whatever occurred after the menstruation is not part of it.'

key_terms.الصُّفْرَة: sufra — yellowish discharge; a color-related concept in Islamic purity law indicating a discharge that may or may not be menstrual blood
key_terms.الْحَيْض: haydh — menstruation; a state of ritual impurity (hadath) that suspends certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Is yellow discharge before or after menstruation considered part of haydh according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) gives a ruling on the status of yellowish vaginal discharge (sufra) in relation to menstruation. The rule is a simple temporal criterion: if the yellow discharge appears before the menstrual period ends, it is considered part of menstruation; if it appears after the period has ended, it is not. This ruling has direct implications for ritual purity (tahara) and the validity of acts of worship such as salat and sawm.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws was asked and I was present, about the woman who sees the yellowness. So heasws said: ‘Whatever was before the menstruation (Haydh), so it is from the menstruation (Haydh), and whatever was after the menstruation (Haydh), so it is not from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was in his presence, about the case of a woman who experiences a discharge of yellowish color. He (the Imam) said, ‘What is before Hayd (menses) is of Hayd (menses) and what is after Hayd (menses) is not Hayd (menses).”’
